messages.author: b1a308a5b9312fbc
messages.subject: inlabru: error in lgcp
parts:
Hi all,

I am fitting a spatial model in inlabru, and in the final steps i encounter the following error that I can not decipher:

Error in as.data.frame.default(x[[i]], optional = TRUE) : cannot coerce class ‘structure("standardGeneric", package =
"methods")’ to a data.frame

I have succeeded at constructing my mesh, and converting my point data and covariates into SpatialPoints, and SpatialPixelDataFrames. I have added pieces of code to clarify:

coords <- data2022_spec[ , c("X", "Y")]           # coordinates
dat    <- data2022_spec[ , 4]                     # data
crs    <- CRS("+init=epsg:31370")                 # proj4string of coords

species22 <- SpatialPointsDataFrame(coords = coords,
                               data        = dat,
                               proj4string = crs)

beaches = st_read("Belgian coast.shp")
Loc = cbind(data2022_spec$X, data2022_spec$Y)
mesh = fm_mesh_2d(boundary = beaches,
                  loc = Loc,
                  max.edge = c(20, 10e3)) 

beach_types = raster("Belgian coast beach types.tif")
spring = raster("SPRING2022.tif")
sand = raster("SAND2022.tif")
spring = as(spring, "SpatialPixelsDataFrame")
sand = as(sand, "SpatialPixelsDataFrame")
beaches = as(beach_types, "SpatialPixelsDataFrame")

matern <- inla.spde2.pcmatern(mesh, prior.range = c(20, 0.05), prior.sigma = c(1, 0.05))

comps <- geometry ~ Intercept(1) + 
  spatialfield(geometry, model = matern)+
  beachtype(beach, model = "factor_contrast") +
  sand(sand, model = "linear") +
  spring(spring, model = "linear") +
 
# fitting
bru_fit <- lgcp(comps, species22, domain = list(geometry = mesh))
summary(bru_fit) # error occurs here

Many thanks in advance!

Charlotte

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] inlabru: error in lgcp
parts:
Your model definition assumes the data to be in sf format (since those have a ”geometry” column), but your species22 object is a SpatialPointsDataFrame. Convert it to sf (e.g. with st_as_sf()).

The covariates should still be ok as SpatialPixels (the covariate evaluator should handle any needed conversion of that). But if you run into a problem with those, convert them to terra format with terra::rast().
Finn
